title: Choose the visual world for izzatjon.dev
question: The roll assigned the Tashkent Metro station world. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Izzatjon Line — Tashkent Metro
options.lineage: Tashkent Metro stations (Kosmonavtlar, Alisher Navoiy), line maps and bilingual station plaques
options.thesis: The portfolio is one metro line: every section is a station, and the last stop is Contact.
options.viewport: A full-width ceramic station plaque with IZZATJON AKBAROV in station lettering, a ceramic medallion portrait, the line map as navigation, and a direction sign to Contact.
options.risk: Turns into a costume if the line map is decoration instead of the working navigation.

raised.raise: Each station owns one committed ceramic field colour, swapped per section, instead of accents on grey.
Race times, summit heights and dates are set as fixed-place departure-board numerals.
Navigation is numbered stations with a clear next exit at the end of every section.
The IA monogram appears once per station as a small found mark, never repeated as wallpaper.

options.label: Chimgan Trail Map
options.lineage: Soviet-era topographic hiking maps of the Chatkal range
options.thesis: The career is drawn as an ascent: an elevation profile is the page spine and each role is a waypoint.
options.viewport: A contour-map field with the name set like a map title, the elevation profile running across the bottom ending at the Contact summit.
options.risk: Mountain topo is a familiar portfolio trope, and it hides the code work behind the hobby.

options.label: Azulejo Station Hall
options.thesis: The portfolio as framed cobalt tile panels walked in order.
options.viewport: A cobalt tile panel naming Izzatjon in a cartouche, the grid seams running through the portrait.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and holds clarity, but a Tashkent hiring manager knows their own metro better than Lisbon’s tiles.
options.risk: Two-colour cobalt limits the light/dark themes and reads foreign to the audience.

options.label: Saul Bass Title Sequence
options.thesis: Each section as a timed cut-paper title card.
options.viewport: A burnt-orange card with a jittering line drawing the name.
options.case: Loses both axes: hiring managers want to scan, not watch a sequence.
options.kept: One committed field colour per act.

options.label: Nixie Laboratory Counter
options.thesis: Every number glows in its own tube.
options.viewport: Tube banks counting years, races and metres.
options.case: Loses both axes: a gadget look with little to say about frontend product work.

options.label: ANSI BBS Nightboard
options.thesis: The portfolio as a text-mode board with numbered menus.
options.viewport: ANSI title art over numbered menu lines.
options.case: Loses both axes: the developer-terminal cliché, unreadable for HR.
options.risk: Exactly the costume the category already wears.

options.label: Art Paul Magazine Program
options.thesis: Each section an issue with a hidden mark.
options.viewport: A serif masthead over two columns with a found mark.
options.case: Loses both axes: an American editorial reference foreign to the audience.

options.label: Coiled Earth Tower
options.viewport: Banded clay courses rising to the name.
options.case: Loses both axes: craft metaphor with no link to code or the visitor.
options.kept: Growth shown as an ordered vertical record.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer portfolio, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role beside a portrait, project cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other developer portfolio by design.
